newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher, in line with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher, in line with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally higher Monday in pursuit of firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.17 to $2.18 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) at 0935 EDT after trading at $2.15 and $2.16 earlier in the session.
The contract, set to expire June 26, settled sharply higher Friday at $2.149.
Early swing cash prices at Henry Hub were talked a few cents higher at $2.17-2.19 per mmBtu.

Summer-like weather in parts of the South is helping to support prices, traders said, as forecasts in Houston called for highs in the mid-90s F through Wednesday amid a fairly high humidity level, Weather Services Corp reported.
However, cool weather is expected to continue in southern California and most of the Midwest and Northwest this week, while near-normal temperatures are forecast for most of the East.
Technically, July resistance was pegged at $2.21, $2.25 and then at $2.37. Support was seen at Friday's low of $2.095, and then at $2.055 and near $2.
In the cash Friday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas was talked little changed in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas held at $2.35-2.40.
